Key Research Thinking Patterns: Experimental Priming of Social Status: Utilizing popularity priming and vignette analysis to isolate causal links between gender prototypicality and perceived social power, demonstrating that physical appearance conformity drives popularity more than behavioral conformity.

Developmental Shift Analysis: Employing open-ended qualitative descriptions and comparative analysis to track the evolution of social prestige metrics from high school (appearance/wealth) to emerging adulthood (prosocial behavior/campus involvement).

Multidisciplinary Disaster Reconstruction: Integrating forensic structural engineering assessments, wind engineering data, and semistructured survivor interviews to correlate human decision-making with physical damage sequences, identifying critical gaps in warning system effectiveness and sheltering efficacy.

Social Support Moderation Modeling: Applying hierarchical regression analysis to distinguish between the impacts of offline versus online social support, revealing that offline family and friend support is foundational for psychological resilience in transgender youth, while online support acts as a moderator for pride outcomes.
Summary Description: Lara Mayeux is a multidisciplinary researcher specializing in the intersection of developmental psychology, social dynamics, and disaster resilience. Her work investigates how gender norms influence adolescent peer status, utilizing experimental priming and longitudinal qualitative methods to map shifts in social prestige from adolescence to emerging adulthood. Concurrently, she applies forensic and wind engineering principles to enhance tornado survivability, linking human behavioral responses with structural performance data. Additionally, she examines psychological resilience in marginalized LGBTQ+ populations, emphasizing the critical role of offline social support systems. Her research bridges social science and engineering to inform interventions for peer victimization, sheltering strategies, and mental health outcomes in high-risk environments.
